Research & the Research Process

Nursing research — meaning, purpose, the research process steps and the role of the nurse in research.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define nursing research and its purposes
  • List the steps of the research process
  • Differentiate quantitative and qualitative research
  • Describe the roles of the nurse in research

In simple words

Research is a careful, controlled way of finding new answers. Nursing research asks questions about nursing so that care is based on evidence, not habit.

Purposes of nursing research

  • Describe and clarify nursing practice
  • Explain and predict patient outcomes
  • Discover new nursing knowledge
  • Test nursing interventions
  • Improve the standard and quality of care
  • Build the professional body of knowledge

Steps of the research process

  1. Formulate the research problem
  2. Review the literature
  3. Formulate objectives and hypotheses
  4. Design the study and select the sample
  5. Develop data collection tools
  6. Collect data ethically
  7. Analyse data
  8. Discuss, conclude and make recommendations
  9. Write the report and disseminate

Types of research

Type Question it answers
Quantitative How many, how much, what effect
Qualitative What does it mean to the person
Experimental Does the intervention cause the change
Non-experimental What is the relationship between variables
Descriptive What is the situation
Correlational Is one variable related to another

🔴 Nursing research is a nursing responsibility

Evaluating and using evidence is part of nursing practice. A nurse who reads, questions and applies evidence improves the patient’s outcome, not only her own knowledge.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Research is organised, purposeful, and designed to answer a question.
  2. Steps: problem, literature, objectives, design, tools, collection, analysis, report.
  3. Quantitative research measures; qualitative research explores meaning.
  4. Ethics comes before data collection, not after.
  5. Findings must be reported so that others can use them.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Evidence-based practice combines research, patient choice and clinical judgement.
  2. Descriptive research describes what exists.
  3. Correlational research tests relationships, not cause.
  4. Generalisation depends on the sample and setting.
  5. Replication confirms findings.

📌 Memory trick

Research cycle: P-L-O-D-C-A-R — Problem, Literature, Objectives, Design, Collect, Analyse, Report.

60-second revision

  • Research is organised, purposeful and search for new knowledge.
  • Nine steps from problem to report.
  • Quantitative vs qualitative; experimental vs non-experimental.
  • Ethics before data collection.
  • Dissemination and application complete the research.

Test yourself

The first step of the research process is:

Answer: B. Formulating the research problem and question comes before design and data collection.

Which research explores what an experience means to a patient?

Answer: B. Qualitative research explores meaning, experience and perception.

Ethical clearance must be obtained:

Answer: B. Ethical approval is needed before any data collection with human participants.

Evidence-based practice uses:

Answer: B. Evidence-based practice combines best research with patient choice and clinical judgement.

The last step of a research study is to:

Answer: C. Findings must be reported and disseminated so that others can use them.
